Run

Needs a kubeconfig with read access to your cluster — either your own, or a dedicated service account scoped with kubernetes/rbac.yaml (this repo):

Scope Access
CNPs, CCNPs, CiliumIdentity, CiliumEndpoint, namespaces get/list/watch
cilium-system (for hubble-relay) pod get/list + port-forward

Nothing GuardBee does writes to the cluster.

Commands

export KUBECONFIG=/path/to/kubeconfig
./guardbee policies -n your-namespace
./guardbee flows -n your-namespace --last 20
./guardbee policies --all-namespaces
./guardbee verdict -n your-namespace --last 50 your-candidate.yaml
./guardbee ui

examples/*.yaml are real catches from the author’s own homelab cluster — they won’t find matching traffic on a different cluster. They’re there to show the kind of regression GuardBee catches, not to run as-is against your own. Point verdict at your own namespace and candidate instead.

Flag conventions

Flag naming follows hubble CLI’s own conventions wherever this tool overlaps with it, so anyone who already knows hubble doesn’t have to relearn a different style here:

Flag Meaning
-n, --namespace One namespace
-A, --all-namespaces Every namespace
-f, --follow Keep tailing until Ctrl+C
--last Ceiling on flows fetched
